To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the major SOD isoform of extracellular fluids and tissues, extracellular SOD (EC-SOD), is produced by a few well-distributed human cell types and that the secreted enzyme binds to the glycocalyx and interstitial matrix of most tissues.
the expression of EC-SUD in cultured cells is restricted to fibroblasts, endothelial cells and glial cells, and that the expression is maintained in long-term cultures.

EC-SOD is produced by a few cell types, such that the enzyme in tissues is produced by a minority of cells, and is secreted by these cells to diffuse subsequently around, to bind to heparin-like ligands in the extracellular matrix, and to protect cells against oxidative stress.
